memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: No Israelite man or woman is to become a shrine prostitute. You must not bring the earnings of a female prostitute or of a male prostitute into the house of the Lord your God to pay any vow, because the Lord your God detests them both. - Deut 23:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God forbids the practice of cult prostitution, which was common in the pagan religions surrounding Israel. In those false religions, sexual immorality was woven into worship itself. God utterly rejects this. His people were not to engage in such practices, nor were they to bring money earned through such sin into His house. God's worship was to be pure, entirely separate from the degrading practices of idolatry.

This shows us how seriously God regards the purity of worship and the dignity of human beings. He would not have His people mixing sexual sin with the worship of the holy God, nor exploiting people's bodies in the name of religion. True worship of the true God honours both His holiness and the dignity He has given to people.

The lasting principle for us is that God calls for pure worship and pure lives. We cannot offer God worship while clinging to sin, nor honour Him while dishonouring the dignity of ourselves or others. The New Testament calls us to glorify God with our bodies, which belong to Him (1 Cor 6:19-20). God is not honoured by worship tainted with unrepentant sin; He desires worship that flows from lives being made holy. Yet He also offers full cleansing and a fresh start to all who turn to Him. Is there any area where you are trying to worship God while holding on to something He calls you to leave behind?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you worship God while clinging to known sin?
2. How do you honour God with your body and your life?
3. What might God be calling you to leave behind?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I want to worship You with a pure heart and a life set apart. Cleanse me and help me honour You in body and spirit. Amen.
